text:
maria: follow-up to RFC - proposing a lightweight regional 'edge cache' to accelerate CP handshakes for private customers. goal: reduce churn on controlplane auth + keep predictable egress IPs when privatelink isn't available.
ajay: quick Q - how is this not just another relay? last thing we need is more heavy proxies.
devon: it's intentionally minimal. no full-stream proxying. stores short-lived tokens, cert blobs, and ACL decisions. answers handshake queries and proxies controlplane API calls only when necessary. designed to be single-purpose and memory-light.
sophia: security first: what are boundaries if cache is compromised? can it mint tokens?
maria: design constraint: cache cannot mint long-lived credentials. it only issues short-lived assertions signed by our KMS, with strict TTL and revocation checks against controlplane before issuing anything beyond a short window. all signing keys are HSM-backed.
ajay: egress preservation: customers need stable source IPs for third-party allowlists. are we reserving per-tenant IPs?
devon: two models discussed: (A) per-tenant ENI/ENI-like lease in customer VPC (preferred for highest isolation), (B) regional shared egress pool we control with per-tenant mapping. MVP: (B) with option for dedicated leases for enterprise.
sophia: cost and capacity concerns. per-tenant IPs blow up cost and routing table complexity. how do we prevent exhaustion?
maria: implement a quota/lease service. default small pool per account, auto-scale only for committed customers. reject new leases when pool exhausted -> signal to sales/ops. lease TTL + renewal to recycle.
ajay: what about IPv6? dualstack expectations creeping up.
devon: scope MVP as IPv4-only. document IPv6 path: require provider support for stable IPv6 source mapping; follow-up spike.
sophia: ops & observability: what metrics and alerts do we need at launch?
maria: minimal metrics: cache_hit_ratio, handshake_latency_ms_p50/p99, lease_in_use, lease_available, revocation_rate. alerts: handshake_errors > 1% sustained 5m, lease_available < 10% for 10m.
ajay: migration plan: existing private customers today use privatelink. do we flip them automatically?
devon: migration is opt-in. registry gets new field egress_mode: privatelink | cache_egress | dedicated_egress. default retains current behavior. provide a migration job for customers who request cache_egress.
sophia: edge cases: what if privatelink exists but DNS resolves to public IPs and agent picks wrong path? precedence rules?
maria: enforce precedence: 1) privatelink endpoint if configured and healthy, 2) private_endpoint, 3) edge_cache, 4) public fallback. we should make agent behavior explicit and observable.
ajay: revocation thundering herd risk when we revoke many tokens. how to avoid slamming controlplane?
devon: coalesce revocations and rate-limit sweeps. cache will subscribe to a revocation stream and process in windows with jitter. also expose a backpressure signal to controlplane so bulk ops can be paced.
sophia: testing matrix before canary: privatelink happy path, cache fallback handshake, token rotation under load, lease exhaustion/resolution, revocation storm simulation, partial region outage.
maria: security items: require attestation of cache image (sigstore), enforce mTLS to controlplane, KMS-backed signing, and redact tokens in logs. threat model doc will enumerate L/R.
ajay: rollout ops: canary in us-west-2 only per infra policy?
infra-bot: deploy-check: any image touching KMS keys requires rolling canary + sigstore proof. schedule canary in us-west-2. ticket created: INFRA-3492.
devon: agent config snippet for precedence and cache TTL:

```
agent:
  egress_priority: [privatelink, private_endpoint, edge_cache, public]
  edge_cache:
    handshake_ttl_s: 30
    cert_ttl_s: 300
```

sophia: docs/UI: registry schema change + a console toggle for egress_mode. need to add explanations and cost warnings for cache_egress.
maria: finance impact: shared egress adds NAT costs; dedicated leases cost more. ajay, can you get a rough cost model for pooled vs dedicated IPs?
ajay: will pair with finance, expect some follow-up.
sophia: last Q - failure semantics: if cache can't reach controlplane, do we fail open?
maria: conservative: fail closed for operations that create or rotate creds. allow read-only cached responses where safe, and return 503s for mutating ops so callers retry. document clearly.
devon: one more - logging: include tenant_id, cache_hit boolean, but redact token_value. retain minimal audit trail for revocations.
infra-bot: note: INFRA-3492 created; must pass canary checklist before regional rollout.
maria: thanks all. I'll draft follow-up RFC with threat model, API contract for registry, migration job outline, and canary plan. please react with thumbs if no blockers.
ajay: :thumbsup: one action - cost model with finance.
sophia: :thumbsup: I'll draft console copy.
devon: :thumbsup: will prototype cache library for agent side.
